title: Microsoft 365 admin center: usage insights for Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go billing
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, published billing requirements and reporting controls are supported. Two navigation details should be clarified, but neither changes the control administrators reach. The briefing appropriately avoids assuming that the planned insights are the documented Credits report.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default of the planned insights view.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat usage insights 492616 Billing usage default enable administrator roles license price; "usage insights" "Copilot" "enable" "license". Read record, overview, setup and Credits report; billing enablement is documented, but not this view's default.

claims.claim: The Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go billing discussed in this briefing is consumption-based.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go service offers a consumption-based option for organizations to access Copilot services, like Microsoft Copilot Chat and SharePoint agents.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go service usage is charged through the configured Azure subscription using the service's Azure meter.
claims.quote: The service gets billed through the Azure subscription that you specified when you set up pay-as-you-go billing. The Azure subscription uses the Azure meter set up for the service.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No licence specific to the planned usage insights view is published, and the record names none.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat usage insights 492616 Billing usage default enable administrator roles license price; "usage insights" "Copilot" "enable" "license". Read record, pay-as-you-go overview and both setup pages; SharePoint prerequisite is product-level, not view-specific.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has published no separate price for the planned usage insights view.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat usage insights 492616 Billing usage default enable administrator roles license price; Copilot Chat usage insights messages credits conversion cost per message meter licensing. Opened overview, meters, setup and Credits report; no price for this view.

claims.claim: Copilot-node pay-as-you-go setup requires at least one SharePoint licence or a licence that includes SharePoint.
claims.quote: The tenant must have at least one SharePoint license, or a license that includes SharePoint.

claims.claim: The cited meters page lists one meter, Copilot Studio, and says agent or custom Copilot usage is billed through its message meter.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio | A billable Copilot Studio message is a request or message sent to the Copilot triggering an action or response. Any agent or custom Copilot usage is billed through Copilot Studio message meter.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited meter's published rate is $0.01 per message.
claims.quote: | Copilot Studio | A billable Copilot Studio message is a request or message sent to the Copilot triggering an action or response. Any agent or custom Copilot usage is billed through Copilot Studio message meter. | $0.01 per message |

claims.claim: The read pages do not state how the planned view's message counts relate to the Credits report and message meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat usage insights messages credits conversion cost per message meter licensing. Read meters, Credits report and billing-rates excerpts; they describe billable units and multi-credit interactions, not a conversion for the planned usage insights view.

claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go overview names establishing usage patterns as a use case.
claims.quote: Establish usage patterns - Admins can understand adoption patterns for new apps to determine if prepaid licenses make financial sense for your organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The Credits report reports metered Copilot Chat consumption for pay-as-you-go billing policies.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot Credits report helps you manage metered consumption costs for Microsoft Copilot Chat. This report gives you visibility into credits used for your Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies.

claims.claim: The Credits report lists credits used per user.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.claim: The Credits report lists credits used per agent.

claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.quote: You can view the Copilot Credits report over the last 7 or 30 days.

claims.quote: During preview, the report displays a maximum of 30 days of Copilot Credits history.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: User-specific details including usernames, display names, groups and sites are hidden in usage reports by default.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.

claims.claim: Billing Policy IDs are anonymised by default in the Credits report.
claims.quote: By default, the Copilot credits report anonymizes the Billing Policy ID, just like the username and display name.

claims.claim: The Credits report attributes usage to the oldest configured billing policy when a user is covered by multiple policies.
claims.quote: If a user is covered by multiple billing policies, this report attributes the usage to the oldest configured billing policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The overview lists Global administrator, Billing administrator, AI administrator and Global reader, with the last read-only, for viewing and managing pay-as-you-go services.
claims.quote: The following administrator roles can view and manage pay-as-you-go services in the Microsoft 365 admin center: Global administrator; Billing administrator; AI administrator; Global reader (read-only access)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn has not documented which roles can open the planned insights view itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat usage insights 492616 Billing usage default enable administrator roles license price. Opened overview, setup, view-cost, Credits report and monitor-spending; roles are given for other surfaces. The record names AI administrators, not a complete permission rule.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go setup and the documented connection tasks require Billing Administrator, AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must have one of the following roles to complete the tasks in this article: Billing Administrator; AI Administrator; Global Administrator

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go setup requires an Azure subscription in the same tenant as Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: You must have an Azure subscription in the same tenant as Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go setup requires a resource group in that Azure subscription.
claims.quote: You must have an Azure resource group in that subscription.

claims.claim: The administrator needs Owner or Contributor rights to the Azure subscription and resource group.
claims.quote: You must have Owner or Contributor rights to the Azure subscription and resource group.

claims.claim: A tenant can create up to 50 billing policies.
claims.quote: You can create up to 50 billing policies for your tenant.

claims.claim: The view-cost page lists Global administrator and Billing administrator for access, fewer roles than the overview lists.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with one of the following administrator roles: Global administrator; Billing administrator

claims.claim: Billing > Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center provides a service-level cost view for Copilot pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Go to Billing > Cost Management. On the Cost Management page, under Service family, you see a service-level view of costs based on Copilot usage.

claims.claim: The disconnection control is at Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services > Microsoft Copilot Chat > Connected.
claims.quote: On the Billing & usage page, select the Pay-as-you-go services tab. Select the service that you want to disconnect. In the Manage billing policy connections panel, select the Connected toggle to turn it off.
claims.fix: Include the named panel in controls[0].ui.path and its rendered row: 'Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services > Microsoft Copilot Chat > Manage billing policy connections > Connected'. The cited page gives this panel before the toggle.

claims.claim: No API equivalent is documented for this classic Copilot Chat billing-policy connection toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta Copilot Chat billing policy connect disconnect pay as you go service API. Read Copilot-node setup and Graph Cost Management overview excerpts; spending-policy service settings are documented, but not this classic billing-policy connection.

claims.claim: Turning the Connected toggle off in Manage billing policy connections disconnects the service.
claims.quote: In the Manage billing policy connections panel, select the Connected toggle to turn it off.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disconnecting a billing policy removes linked users' access to metered agents in that Copilot service.
claims.quote: Upon disconnection, users linked to that billing policy lose access to the metered agents in the Copilot service.

claims.claim: The Credits report is reached at Reports > Usage > Reports > Microsoft Copilot > Credits; prose omits the second Reports heading.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Reports. ... Select Usage. On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Credits.

claims.claim: No API equivalent for this Microsoft 365 Credits report's per-agent and per-billing-policy view is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot Credits report per agent billing policy Microsoft Graph API get report; "Copilot Credits report" "API" "billing policy". Read Credits report, Graph usage overview, and Power Platform download tutorial; the latter exposes PPAC reports, not this report.

claims.claim: Show all reveals Reports when Reports is not visible in navigation.
claims.quote: If you don't see Reports, select Show all, and then select Reports.

claims.claim: The billing-policy spending view is at Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage > Billing policies > billing policy > Budget > Spending.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Cost management ... select Classic Billing & usage. On the Billing policies tab, select a billing policy. In the side panel, select the Budget tab. The Spending option displays data for the current month

claims.claim: No API equivalent for the classic billing-policy Budget and Spending view is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot billing policy budget spending API Graph PowerShell. Read Copilot-node setup, budget-page search excerpts and Graph Cost Management overview excerpts; Graph credit spending-policy alerts do not document the classic billing-policy budget view.

claims.claim: Spending displays data for the current month.
claims.quote: The Spending option displays data for the current month

claims.claim: Spending includes a chart of the last six months.
claims.quote: Includes a chart that displays data for the last six months.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A billing-policy budget triggers email notifications.
claims.quote: When you set a budget amount, it triggers email notifications based on your organization's spending relative to that limit.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The budget is not enforced and does not stop usage or prevent spending beyond it.
claims.quote: The system doesn't enforce the budget or prevent your organization from exceeding it. Usage can continue uninterrupted even after the budget is surpassed

claims.where: Governance controls; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: No documented switch turns the planned usage insights view itself on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat usage insights 492616 Billing usage default enable administrator roles license price; "usage insights" "Copilot" "enable" "license". Read roadmap, overview, setup, Credits report and monitor-spending; controls enable billing, not this view.

claims.claim: The Cost Management API documents credit usage reports by user, security group, governed service and funding class.
claims.quote: Use the Cost Management API usage reports to analyze consumption of Copilot Credits by user, security group, governed service, or funding class.

claims.claim: Those Graph usage reports do not document a per-agent view.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot Credits report per agent billing policy Microsoft Graph API get report. Read the complete Graph usage-reports-overview: report dimensions are user, group, service, funding and raw service/session detail, with no per-agent report.

claims.claim: Copilot > Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services is a documented route to review policy service connections.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Billing & usage. On the Billing & usage page, select the Pay-as-you-go services tab.
claims.fix: Replace the checklist path with 'Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services > Microsoft Copilot Chat', matching the route at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot. The other cited setup page still gives the older route.

claims.claim: The connection and budget controls govern the Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go billing underlying the planned view, not the view itself.
claims.quote: After you create a billing policy, you must link it to a Copilot service, like Microsoft Copilot Chat or SharePoint agents. ... As an admin, you can add a budget limit to a billing policy

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The record describes a reporting view and describes no resulting action taken by an agent.
claims.quote: AI administrators can view usage insights to inform agent management decisions. This feature displays the cost and number of messages in total and per agent. Cost and usage details can be filtered by billing policy and date range.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no new data access or setting that changes users' capabilities.
claims.quote: As you enable M365 Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go billing, AI administrators can view usage insights to inform agent management decisions. This feature displays the cost and number of messages in total and per agent.

claims.claim: The documented Cost Management API usage reports are beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.
